title: The three economic questions

draft.title: The three economic questions
card: Resources are limited, so no economy can make everything people want. Every economy must make choices about how to use its resources.
which goods and services to make, and how much of each. Making more homes may mean making fewer roads.
which resources and methods to use. A bakery could use many workers or more machines to make bread.
who will receive the goods and services. This decides how what is made is shared among people.
draft.remember: Scarcity forces choices: what to make, how to make it and who gets it.

a.q: A government must decide whether to build a new hospital or a new sports stadium. Which economic question is this?
a.why: The choice is about which goods and services to make with limited resources, so it is the question of what to produce. It is not how to produce, because it is not about the methods used to build.
a.clue: Is the choice about which thing to make, or about the method?

b.q: Kai runs a furniture factory in Hobart. He decides to use machines instead of more workers to make chairs. Which question is Kai answering?
opts: What to sell at a lower price
b.why: Kai is choosing which resources and methods to use, so he is answering how to produce. It is not what to produce, because he has already chosen to make chairs and is deciding only about the method.
b.clue: Kai has already chosen chairs. What is he deciding now?
